extracted.intended_audience: aspiring stand-up comedians and comedy writers
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, formulaic workbook-style approach to writing and evaluating stand-up jokes focused on setups, attitude, authenticity, and word choice to maximize audience laughter. Uses exercises and a short rubric to iterate joke drafts for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup authenticity / seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Setups are usually very serious and authentic; they have a ring of truth and honesty and establish a foundation for the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the workbook: setups should feel authentic and serious (truth-grounded). They establish the foundation for the punchline — an effective setup reads as honest, with a ring of truth. Exercise implication: find real, serious details to ground the setup. Anti-pattern: flippant or insincere setups that fail to build credible context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear attitude (emotional point of view)
rubrics_metrics.description: A funny attitude for a joke = the comedian's emotional perspective on the topic; attitude words are the tools to get really big laughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether there is a distinct emotional POV on the topic. Guidance warns that "jokes without attitude end up sounding too literary — humorous but not funny enough to get big laughs." Use attitude words deliberately to heighten the joke. Anti-pattern: neutral or bland delivery that reads as merely clever rather than emotionally invested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic voice / uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Find your 'authentic voice' — the true source of comedy; the comedian should sound like an authentic voice (not generic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for signs that the material springs from the performer's unique perspective rather than stock observations. The workbook emphasizes embarrassing truths about oneself and reluctant admissions as sources of authenticity. Exercises prompt performers to mine personal material to avoid sounding generic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of an embarrassing truth or reluctant admission
rubrics_metrics.description: Embarrassing truths about oneself are gold; reluctant admissions reveal genuine comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the joke contains an element of personal embarrassment or a reluctant admission that exposes vulnerability — these are highlighted as high-value comedic material. Exercises include coming up with embarrassing truths and reluctant admissions. Anti-pattern: purely observational jokes without any revealed vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word sharpness / immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the words sharp enough to capture attention quickly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes should use sharp, concise wording to grab the audience immediately. The workbook notes that the audience "makes up its mind quickly," so each joke must capture attention then deliver the laugh. Revise for brevity, punchy phrasing, and strong word choices that speed audience comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of creative techniques (half-truth mashups, redefinitions, acronyms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques include half-truth mashups combining different identities, redefining industry terms humorously, and transforming acronyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specified exercises are recommended methods to generate comic premises and twists. When evaluating, consider whether the joke employs one of these inventive strategies effectively (e.g., surprising mashup logic, clever redefinition, or a transformed acronym). Examples/exercises in the workbook encourage practicing these devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement / timing (capture then laugh)
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience makes up its mind quickly; every joke is important to capture attention, then make them laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the joke's ability to both seize the audience's attention early and convert that attention into laughter. This includes pacing, setup economy, and punchline payoff. Guidance implies iterative testing/rewriting during performance to ensure immediate engagement; anti-pattern is slow-building lines that lose audience buy-in before the payoff.
